The 2024 disclosure confirms the Firm adopted the Reference Rate Reform update, extending the relief period to 2024, applying expedients for LIBOR references, and noting no impact on financial statements. They cover the same specific accounting update and its application.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of FASB ASU 2022-06 deferring Topic 848 sunset date
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi adopted FASB ASU No. 2022-06 upon issuance, which deferred the sunset date of the Reference Rate Reform relief guidance (Topic 848) to December 31, 2024, allowing the company to transition remaining contracts and maintain hedge accounting; the adoption did not impact 2022 financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan Chase (MS) and Citigroup (C) disclose the adoption of the Reference Rate Reform accounting update (Topic 848) extending relief through December 31, 2024. Similar to MS, which states there was 'no impact to the Firm's financial statements upon issuance' of the update, Citi also reports that its adoption of ASU No. 2022-06 'did not impact financial results in 2022'. Both entities utilize the optional expedients to manage contracts referencing discontinued benchmarks like LIBOR.

sentences.text: The Firm has adopted the Reference Rate Reform accounting update, which extends the period of time entities can utilize the reference rate reform relief guidance from December 31, 2022 to December 31, 2024.
There was no impact to the Firm's financial statements upon issuance of this accounting standard update.

On December 21, 2022, the FASB issued ASU No. 2022-06, Reference Rate Reform (Topic 848): Deferral of the Sunset Date of Topic 848, which extends the period of time preparers can utilize the reference rate reform relief guidance.
The ASU was adopted by Citi upon issuance and did not impact financial results in 2022.
